content.comment_body: I have a few questions about the [product_name] Web Editor and [product_name] Web Server. I'm new to the [product_name] web server, so I appreciate your patience. Could someone tell me the [article_no] for the [product_name] Web Editor license? Is there a separate license for the Web Editor compared to the Web Server? Thank you in advance.

The [product_name] web server comes integrated with the firmware of the [product_name] controller with [version_no]. Devices with firmware versions [version_no] and [version_no] only have a basic web server that simulates the device's display and buttons in a web browser. The latest controller with firmware [version_no] introduces an extended web server that lets you create custom web pages. To make these custom pages, use the [product_name] Web Editor software and upload them to the device via an mSD card.
Is it possible to display all digital and analog signals? How can analog signals be presented?
Your questions are a bit broad. Where are you looking to view your signals—on the basic web server or the extended one?
I'm asking specifically about the extended web server. I have many analog and digital signals from several controllers. Is there any way to keep a data history?

As mentioned, the extended web server is part of the controller's firmware and can only show values from its own device. To display data from other controllers, you first need to transfer those values to this one over the network.
Are you saying that only one controller can be connected in this setup?
Each controller has its own web server. There isn’t a shared web server that allows access to all controllers together.

You can use one controller as a data collector. Send data from other controllers to it via network input/output. Then you can use this controller to display various data on the web. It's also possible to log network inputs from other controllers into a CSV file for data history.

Does this mean only one port can be opened for a static IP in the Web Editor? Or can I display other controllers on different static IPs, but only one IP is accessible at a time, so switching between them must be done manually?
Also, for this application, how do I set it up and are there any restrictions on the number of analog and digital signals I can link to one controller?

Use Network Input/Output to connect controllers. You can either "pull" data from other controllers into a designated data collector or "push" data from each one to the collector's VM memory. For each display, you can show a maximum of eight values at once, so you may need to use multiple pages for different data sets. Not certain if custom displays allow for more; haven't tested that yet. The port setting cannot be changed on the controller, but you can configure port mapping on your router/firewall to access different controllers in your LAN from the web using separate ports, e.g. port 80 for one device, 81 for another, and so on.

Thank you for your helpful answer. I'll come back with some specific questions, and I appreciate your patience: 1) Is extra hardware required for these connections? 2) My controllers aren't on the same LAN; they'll be connected via VPN to a PC. Will this setup still work? 3) How can I identify which signal belongs to which controller when collecting all data centrally?

1) Is additional hardware needed? The devices need to be directly accessible by fixed IP. 2) If controllers are connected via VPN, direct fixed IP access between devices is still necessary. 3) To know which signal is from which controller, configure the network input/output blocks in the software. Assign different addresses for each controller's data, record which address corresponds to which signal, and use that info for display. For pulling data, specify the IP and address to retrieve each value.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering limitations with the [product_name] Web Editor and web server around displaying and logging data, especially from multiple controllers. The web server is limited to showing data from its own device, and centralized monitoring requires network data transfer to a collector device. There is some confusion about licensing and hardware requirements for configuring multi-controller setups.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want the capability to centrally monitor and log both analog and digital signals from multiple controllers, track their history, and have clarity about licensing and technical requirements for integrated connections.
